newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken realigns top management.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken realigns top management.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc. said Thursday it realigned its top management, adding that it was not satisfied with sales growth in its Boston Market stores.
It said aggressive discounts used to build its lunch business had cut into its core dinner sales business.
Shares of Boston Chicken, one of the pioneers of the home replacement meal concept and one of the hottest inital public offerings of the decade, fell sharply in heavy trading.
The stock lost about 10 percent at the opening of trading, shedding $1.675 to $16.50 with over 4.6 mllion shares traded by mid-morning on Nasdaq, where it was the most active issue.

Boston Chicken said President and Chief Executive Larry Zwain resigned but will remain on the board. Scott Beck and Saad Nadhir will share the office of chairman and Beck will retain his position as chief executive.
Formerly, Beck was chairman and CEO and Nadhir was vice chairman. The two will refocus on the core business, home meal replacement, the company said.

"The issue is that we've begun to see this lunch-driven discounting negatively impact our dinner sales," Beck said. "We are going to refocus the brand on what made Boston Market so successful in the first place, serving the home meal replacement market."
He added: "Dinner will be the centrepiece, with lunch as a sideline as opposed to lunch as a centrepiece, with dinner as a sideline."

The organisational changes will not involve Boston Market store-level employees, Einstein/Noah Bagel Corp. or affect any of the services Boston Chicken provides to Einstein/Noah Bagel, the company said.
Boston Chicken currently runs or franchises 1,159 Boston Market stores and owns a majority interest in Einstein/Noah Bagel Corp.
